prompt: Consider the statement: "If it rains on Saturday, then the bridge inspection is postponed." What is the hypothesis?

choices.label: The bridge inspection is not postponed

hint: A conditional has two halves. One follows "if," the other follows "then."

hints.text: A conditional has two halves. One follows "if," the other follows "then."
The hypothesis is the "if" part — the condition that gets things started.
The hypothesis is "it rains on Saturday."

explanation: A conditional statement has the form "if $p$, then $q$."
The hypothesis is $p$, the part right after "if"; the conclusion is $q$, the part after "then."
Here the hypothesis is "it rains on Saturday," and the conclusion is "the bridge inspection is postponed."

alternativeExplanations.title: Cause and effect
steps: The hypothesis is the setup, the thing that might happen: rain.
The conclusion is what follows from it: the postponed inspection. Setup first, result second.
